philosophers_stone.name: Philosopher's Stone
philosophers_stone.lore: The alchemists named their quest the Great Work and wrote that it passes through three colours, the blackening, the whitening and at last the reddening, in which the Stone appears. Zosimos of Panopolis sought it in Roman Egypt, copyists declared that Nicolas Flamel had made it in Paris, and the Emerald Tablet, ascribed to Hermes Trismegistus, gives all the method in one line: that which is above is like that which is below. Yet none of them ever held this. It is red, heavier than gold and warm as a living hand, and it shows truly whatever it is carried past. Abaddon kept it in the Pit because its last change needs sunlight.

bronze_bull.name: Bronze Bull Idol
bronze_bull.lore: King Minos prayed to Poseidon for a sign that Crete was his to rule, and the god sent a white bull walking out of the surf, which was to be given back to him in sacrifice. But Minos thought it too fair to kill and offered a lesser beast, and for this Poseidon punished the king's house with the birth of the Minotaur Asterion, whom the Labyrinth was built to hide. This little bull of bronze, worn smooth by centuries of hands, smells faintly yet of sea-foam, and it still wants to be given back at sacred water.

eye_of_graeae.name: Eye of the Graeae
eye_of_graeae.lore: Deino, Enyo and Pemphredo, the three Grey Sisters, were born old and had but one eye and one tooth among them, which went from hand to hand. Perseus waited until the eye was passing between two, when all three were blind, and seized it, and would not restore it until they told him the road to Medusa. It is milky and cold as a sea-stone, and it watches still from within a pack. The gods rewarded that cunning deed at a place sacred to Athena, and it may be that they would do so again.

cats_footstep.name: Sound of a Cat's Footstep
cats_footstep.lore: Twice the wolf Fenrir burst the iron chains of the gods, and then Odin sent to the dwarves, who asked for six things, of which the first was the noise that a cat makes in walking. They used all that there was of it, and that, as Snorri gravely records, is why the step of a cat has been silent ever since. It is held in this vial of glass, which makes no sound when it is shaken.

womans_beard.name: Beard of a Woman
womans_beard.lore: The beard of a woman was the second of the six things that the dwarves of Svartalfheim wrought into the fetter Gleipnir, and the old storyteller who set down the recipe bade his hearer prove it by looking about the world, where women have no beards because the dwarves took them all. This twist of fine threads is like hair, and the eye slips from it continually.

mountain_root.name: Root of a Mountain
mountain_root.lore: One would think that a mountain must be rooted as a tree is, yet those who dig beneath one find only more stone. The reason, as the Norsemen tell, is that the dwarves pulled up every root there was to bind the wolf Fenrir. This gnarled tendril, grey and cool and a very little pliant, was left lying upon the workshop floor.

fish_breath.name: Breath of a Fish
fish_breath.lore: Fishes draw no air, and no one has seen the breath of a fish hang upon a winter morning. Yet in the reckoning of the Norse there was once such a thing, until the dwarves gathered every whit of it for the cord that holds the wolf. This sealed bubble smells of deep water and cold currents, and it turns slowly, as though it sought the surface still.

bird_spittle.name: Spittle of a Bird
bird_spittle.lore: Last of all that went to the making of Gleipnir was the spittle of a bird, and here is one bright drop that keeps its shape and glistens without any light. The birds gave up theirs that Fenrir might be bound, and where he lies with a sword propping his jaws he drools now so greatly as to fill a river, which the Norse call Van.

bear_sinew.name: Sinews of a Bear
bear_sinew.lore: The dwarves asked for the sinews of a bear, the cords that carry feeling through all that mighty body, and wove them into the wolf's fetter with five other things that are no longer in the world. This pale thread is of a kind between nerve and tendon, and it twitches now and again as if it felt some movement, for it senses what its bearer cannot.

gleipnir.name: Gleipnir
gleipnir.lore: Leyding was the name of the first chain that the gods made for Fenrir, and Dromi, twice as strong, of the second, and he snapped them both. The third is this ribbon, as smooth and soft as silk, which the dwarves made from six things that are in the world no longer. The wolf suspected a trick and would not be bound unless a god laid a hand between his jaws for a pledge, and Tyr alone came forward. It tightened the more as the wolf strove, and all the gods laughed save Tyr, who lost his hand. From that day to this the ribbon has never been broken.

leather_scrap.name: leather scrap
leather_scrap._weight_note: Five pounds a scrap, fifty for all ten: half a STR-10 hero's load, carried from floor 5 to floor 79 (winning-build plan 2026-11-13 section 3.7). The lore says nothing of what they are for; only Recall Lore does (data/hints.json).
leather_scrap.lore: When a cobbler cuts a sole he trims away the stiff corner at toe or heel, and this is such a piece of shoe leather. It is thick and heavy, as hard as a board, too rigid to patch armour and too tough to sew, so that it is of no use to anyone.

seal_of_wrath.name: Seal of Wrath
seal_of_wrath.lore: John of Patmos beheld in heaven a scroll that was sealed with seven seals, and woe followed at the breaking of each. The Pit likewise has seven, and this blood-red disc, hot as a coin left in the fire and reeking of brimstone, was in the keeping of the first of its guardians, from whose body it could not be taken until the demon was dead.

seal_of_pestilence.name: Seal of Pestilence
seal_of_pestilence.lore: Tradition gives to the rider on the white horse a crown, a bow and the name of Pestilence, and sends him forth conquering, and the demon who bore this seal did the like work in the darkness below. It is a disc of sickly green that weeps some foulness and makes the air hum as with a cloud of flies, and it is so rotten that it will break in the first hand that lifts it.

seal_of_famine.name: Seal of Famine
seal_of_famine.lore: Upon a black horse sits the third rider of the Apocalypse with a pair of scales in his hand, while a voice names his prices: a day's wage for a measure of wheat. This withered disc, coloured like dead grain, is one of the seven locks upon the Abyss, and it is so withered that it will break in the first hand that lifts it.

seal_of_war.name: Seal of War
seal_of_war.lore: To the rider of the red horse was given a great sword, and power to take peace from the earth so that men should kill one another. This disc of rusty red, graven with crossed blades, trembles at the memory of the shouting and the standards and the field when all was over, and a demon wore it as the badge of his office, which was the warding of the Pit.

seal_of_death.name: Seal of Death
seal_of_death.lore: Of the fourth rider John wrote: behold a pale horse, and his name that sat on him was Death, and Hell followed with him. This pale disc is cold as a headstone in January, and it will break in the first hand that lifts it. The demon who carried it is dead, yet the seal is no less baleful than while he lived.

seal_of_earthquake.name: Seal of the Earthquake
seal_of_earthquake.lore: At the opening of the sixth seal John saw a great earthquake, when the sun turned black as sackcloth, the moon became as blood, and every mountain and island was moved out of its place. This cracked grey disc shivers where it lies and the stone about it groans, as if it remembered that command and waited only for a hand to break it.

seal_of_silence.name: Seal of Silence
seal_of_silence.lore: When the Lamb opened the seventh seal there was silence in heaven for about half an hour, and then the seven trumpets were given out. This pale disc of silver swallows sound so that even breath is muffled near it, and it is the last and worst lock of the Pit, for in its quiet those trumpets wait to be blown.

scales_of_michael.name: Scales of Michael
scales_of_michael.lore: With the cry 'Who is like God?', which is the meaning of his name, Michael cast the Dragon out of heaven. The painters show him with a sword in one hand and in the other a pair of scales, in which he weighs the souls at Judgment while a devil seeks to tip the pan, and these are those scales. The Book of Revelation names Abaddon, the Destroyer, as king of the locusts of the Abyss, and when he opens the Pit the Host will answer these scales, so that for every locust that rises an angel comes down.

cursed_lodestone.name: Cursed Lodestone
cursed_lodestone.lore: Thales of Miletus held that the lodestone must have a soul, since it moves iron without touching it, but this one has a will besides. It is a great black stone that drinks the light about it, as heavy as a small anvil. A knight who lay dying begged a stranger to carry it for his wife's sake, and by its curse it is bound to anyone who takes it up freely and cannot be set down. Only an altar will break that bond, and even then the promise would still be owed.

sealed_dispatch.name: Sealed Dispatch
sealed_dispatch.lore: A courier bore this iron-bound case of scrolls as far as he was able, and with his last breath he begged that another would finish the journey. It is closed with the wax seal of the City Watch and holds the stations of the companies that defend a city under siege, so that thousands of lives hang upon its reaching the sergeant at the post below. It is heavy, and to its own weight is added the weight of a promise.

palladium.name: Palladium
palladium.lore: The Trojans held that this wooden image of armed Athena, small enough to be carried beneath one arm, fell from heaven at the feet of Ilus their founder, and it was prophesied that Troy could not fall while it stayed within the walls. Therefore Odysseus and Diomedes crept in by night and stole it, and only then was it worth their while to build the Horse. The goddess of sound counsel in war favours still whoever bears her likeness, and shows to the bearer the way down through stone and darkness alike.

tablet_of_destinies.name: Tablet of Destinies
tablet_of_destinies.lore: He who held the Tablet of Destinies was master of what must be, and Enlil, chief of the gods of Sumer, wore it on his breast and laid it by only when he bathed. Anzu, the lion-headed bird of storm who guarded his door, watched for that hour and flew off with it to the mountains, and every decree of heaven fell silent until Ninurta hunted him down with arrows and brought it home. In each place it lets its bearer refuse one verdict: a wrong answer is unsaid, the clay cracks a little further, and a different question is asked.

vidars_sandal.name: Vidar's Sandal
vidars_sandal.lore: Vidar, the silent son of Odin, has a shoe that has been in the making since the world began. It is pieced from the scraps that cobblers trim from the toes and heels of every shoe, and for that reason the Norsemen say that one who would help the gods should cast those scraps away. At Ragnarok, when the wolf Fenrir has swallowed Odin, Vidar will set this shoe upon the lower jaw of the wolf, take the upper jaw in his hand and rend him asunder.
vidars_sandal._design_note: MEGA-SECRET quest reward. AC is modest (1 + leather material bonus) — the value is the instant-kill on Fenrir, not the defensive line. peak_weight 0.0 ensures it never natural-spawns; the altar assembly path is the only way in. Code references: src/game_combat.py:1292-1311 (instant-kill trigger), src/game_divine.py:499-521 (altar assembly), src/dungeon.py:2145-2154 (altar carve). See tools/balance/systems/bosses_and_quests.md §Fenrir Quest Layer 2.

pandoras_box.name: Pandora's Box

chaos_table.desc: Plague released -- you and all enemies in sight are poisoned for 30 turns.
Toil released -- enemies in sight gain +1 attack chain capacity; you lose 1 for 50 turns.
Strife released -- a random monster in sight turns hostile to all others (and you).
Famine released -- hunger meter drops 25%.
Madness released -- a random stat drops by 1 for 100 turns.
Lies released -- one unidentified item gains a false flavor description for 100 turns.
Old Age released -- DEX -2 for 50 turns.
Despair released -- lose 5 SP and cannot SP-cast for 20 turns.
Tempest released -- a lightning bolt strikes a random tile in sight (4d6).
Polymorph one -- a random hostile in sight becomes a mouse for 30 turns.
Foresight kept -- you gain Clairvoyant for 50 turns.
Toil-mastery -- +1 chain capacity on all quizzes for 50 turns.
Memory of Eden -- +1 to a random stat for 50 turns.
Friendship -- the nearest hostile monster is charmed for 30 turns.
Curiosity rewarded -- all unidentified items in inventory are identified.
Beauty unleashed -- monsters within 2 tiles cannot attack you for 5 turns.
Health restored -- HP and SP refilled to full.
Foreknowledge -- full mini-map for current floor revealed.
Strength of will -- 3 turns of Protected and 50 turns of Hasted.
Hope -- permanent +1 to a random stat.

chaos_table_failure_skew.description: On quiz failure, re-roll a 1d20 with the lower half mapped to negative effects (rolls 1-14 = rolls 1-14 of chaos_table) and rolls 15-20 mapped to chaos_table rolls 11-16. The 'Hope' roll (20) is unavailable on failure -- you cannot grasp Hope by sloppy theology.

pandoras_box.lore: It was Pandora whom Zeus sent, bearing a jar, to Epimetheus, though his brother Prometheus had warned him to take no gift from Olympus. Hesiod, who first told the tale, calls it a pithos, which is a jar of clay as tall as a man, but more than two thousand years afterward the scholar Erasmus rendered the word amiss and it has been a box ever since. She lifted the lid, and sickness, toil and every sorrow flew out over the earth before she could clap it shut with Hope alone left caught beneath the rim. This one is small, sealed with wax and cord and painted with fleeing figures.

aladdins_lamp.name: Aladdin's Lamp

item.desc: Wish for an item. The player names a category (weapon / armor / shield / accessory / artifact / wand / scroll / spellbook / potion). The djinn generates a random item of that category at ONE TIER ABOVE the current floor's normal loot tier. For 'artifact', the djinn produces a random non-quest artifact not currently in the player's inventory.

power.desc: Wish for a power. Choose ONE: permanent +1 to any single stat (player picks STR/CON/DEX/INT/WIS/PER, no cap override), OR a permanent status immunity (player picks from the immunity list).

entity.desc: Wish for a named entity. Choose ONE: summon a powerful ally for 50 turns (paladin, archmage, or holy warrior -- equivalent to a tier-5 charmed monster), OR reveal the location, name, and weakness of the next boss/unique-monster on a future floor.

wish_fallback_effects.desc: A random item from a randomly chosen category appears, but at ONE TIER BELOW the current floor's normal loot tier.
Permanent +1 to a RANDOM stat (not player's choice).
100 turns of a random temporary status immunity (poison, paralysis, fear, sleep, blindness, or confusion).
Summon a random tier-3 ally for 25 turns (half normal duration).
Reveal only the next boss's floor location -- no name, no weakness.

aladdins_lamp.lore: The tale of Aladdin is in none of the old Arabic books of the Thousand and One Nights, but Hanna Diyab, a storyteller of Syria, told it in Paris in 1709 to the Frenchman Antoine Galland, who wrote it among the others. In it a sorcerer out of the far west sent a tailor's idle son into a cave for a lamp that he called worthless, and this dented lamp of tarnished brass would indeed fetch nothing at market. Yet a jinni is bound within it, patient and exact, who grants a single wish to a worthy hand, and half of one to an unworthy hand.

soul_sphere.name: Soul Sphere
soul_sphere._doc_sphere: The six Soul Spheres (pet_system.sphere_spec). 'sphere': what hatches: tier 1/2/3 hatches at hatch_level 1, 25 or 55 (a newborn, its first evolution, its final form); 'family' guarantees one of the family's own companions. The SPHERE decides, never the floor. 'floor_spawn_chance': its chance per floor, by floor band (dungeon.spawn_items rolls ONE number for all six). Trader stock and prices: data/traders.json, data/item_worth.json share_by_id. A sphere is never cursed (can_be_cursed false, buc_known true); its KIND is learned by identifying it or by throwing one (as a thrown potion teaches), and it looks the same either way (its art is the item; the unidentified name describes that look).
soul_sphere.lore: Within a globe of smoky glass, caged about with dark iron, a pale wisp of soul-light lies curled in sleep. If you throw it the sleeper will wake at your side as a newborn companion, which is most often a creature of one of the four elements, and once in a long while is someone you know from home.

greater_soul_sphere.name: Greater Soul Sphere
greater_soul_sphere.lore: Bright silver cages this globe of smoky glass, and the soul-light in it burns like a little blue star, for the spirit that sleeps here has grown already into its first true form. When it is thrown it wakes ready for battle, having learned the first of its special skills, and most often it is a creature of the elements, though once in a long while it is someone you know from home.

master_sphere.name: Master Sphere
master_sphere.lore: Only a handful of these spheres were made by the masters of the old art of binding, and most lie here still in the deep places. Each is of crystal, caged in four hoops of silver beneath a little crown, and so full of soul-light that the eye can scarcely bear it, for the spirit within is full grown, in its final form, with every skill that its kind can learn.

hearth_sphere.name: Hearth Sphere
hearth_sphere.lore: Warm as a stone from beside the hearth at home is this sphere of smoky glass in its cage of iron trimmed with gold. The wisp within is no stranger, for it is always one of the family's own companions, come down into the dark to find you. But if every one of them is at your side already, it is a newborn creature of the elements that answers.

greater_hearth_sphere.name: Greater Hearth Sphere
greater_hearth_sphere.lore: A light burns warm and steady within this smoky glass and its cage of gold-trimmed silver, like a lamp set in the window for one who is coming home late. Here sleeps one of the family's own companions, grown already into its first true form, and if every one of them is at your side already, a grown creature of the elements will answer instead.

master_hearth_sphere.name: Master Hearth Sphere
master_hearth_sphere.lore: One of the family's own companions has come a very long way to stand beside you, and waits at the height of its strength, in its final form. The crystal that holds it, with four gold-trimmed hoops of silver and a little golden crown, blazes with warm light. If every one of them is beside you already, a creature of the elements in its final form will answer instead.

unusual_soul_sphere.name: Unusual Soul Sphere
unusual_soul_sphere.lore: An unusual soul sphere. Its colors are black and silver. It pulses with a powerful energy...

lions_thorn.name: Lion's Thorn
lions_thorn.lore: Androcles, a runaway slave, once drew such a thorn from a lion's paw in a cave of Africa, as Aulus Gellius tells, and when the two met again years later upon the sand of the Circus, before all Rome, the lion remembered him. This black thorn, as long as a finger, came from the paw of a lion who suffered it to be drawn out more patiently than anyone would expect. The memory of lions is long, and the thorn smells of him still.

cuthberts_gospel.name: Saint Cuthbert's Gospel
cuthberts_gospel.lore: In the coffin of Cuthbert of Lindisfarne, the shepherd who was made a bishop and would gladly have remained a hermit, there lay this Gospel of John, small enough for a pocket and bound in red leather worked with a vine. When the longships came the monks lifted coffin and book together and bore them from place to place for seven years, and the last bearer has sent the book down to a chapel where his brothers wait. Though it is worth much money to the wrong people, it was given into your hand upon a promise.

wats_oil_flask.name: Wat's Oil Flask
wats_oil_flask.unidentified_name: a dented flask of lamp oil
wats_oil_flask.lore: For sixty years Wat Rowe has lit the seven lamps upon the Long Stair, that pilgrims might see their feet, but his old knees will carry him now to six and no farther. The seventh stands at the bottom, and last winter two pilgrims fell in the darkness beneath it. He had this dented tin flask of oil warm in his lap, and it is his saying that nobody remembers who lit a lamp, but everybody remembers falling.

olifant.name: The Olifant
olifant.unidentified_name: a great ivory horn bound in gold
olifant.lore: Roland bore this horn, carved from a single elephant's tusk and bound with gold. At Roncevaux, when the Saracens came over the hills in their thousands, his friend Oliver begged him three times to sound it while Charlemagne was near enough to turn back, and three times Roland was too proud. Only when the rear guard was dying did he blow, so hard that his temples burst, and Charlemagne heard it thirty leagues off and came galloping back to find them all dead. Since help that is called from far away comes late, you should blow it before the fight, and then give ground and hold on until it comes. The mouthpiece is cracked along its length, and Roland asked that it be blown at the last gate, so that the rear guard should be remembered.

_meta.sources: The Song of Roland (Oxford manuscript), laisses 83-85 and 133-135: Oliver's three pleas, the horn heard thirty leagues off, Ganelon's 'it is nothing', Naimes' 'he is in battle', the host turning back. The power is in data/horns.json; the lore retold 2026-11-16 so it teaches the legend's lesson (Grokipedia, Song of Roland; Wikipedia, The Song of Roland).

robin_hoods_horn.name: Robin Hood's Horn
robin_hoods_horn.unidentified_name: a hunting horn on a green baldric
robin_hoods_horn.lore: Robin Hood wore this hunting horn upon a baldric of Lincoln green, and in the ballads his yeomen came out of the greenwood at the sound of it. He blew it when Little John tumbled him from a narrow bridge into the brook, and when the curtal friar threw him in the river, and last of all at Kirklees in three weak blasts, when Little John came too late to save him. For a fair bout upon the bridge he hung it round your neck, and if you blow it once, in need, his Merry Men will come.

_meta.sources: Child Ballads 125 (Robin Hood and Little John), 123 (Robin Hood and the Curtal Friar), 120 (Robin Hood's Death); A Gest of Robyn Hode. Grokipedia (Little John, Merry Men, Robin Hood's Death), Wikipedia (the three ballads). The power is in data/horns.json.

arthurs_bugle.name: Arthur's Bugle
arthurs_bugle.unidentified_name: an old bugle-horn on a baldric
arthurs_bugle.lore: At Sewingshields by the Roman Wall the folk tell of a farmer who followed his ball of thread into the hall beneath the hill, where Arthur sleeps with his queen, his knights and his hounds, and where this bugle lay upon a table. He drew the sword and they woke, and he cut the garter, but then his courage failed and he sheathed the sword, so that they slept once more, while Arthur cursed the day of the man who never blew the bugle-horn. You blew it, and Arthur gave it back to you against your hour of greatest need. Blow it once more, and the sleepers will come.

_meta.sources: The Sewingshields legend: Hodgson, History of Northumberland (1840); The Denham Tracts vol. 2 (1895), pp. 125-27, via D. L. Ashliman, Sleeping Hero Legends; pantheon.org, Sewingshields Castle. No Grokipedia page (searched). The power is in data/horns.json.

gjallarhorn.name: Gjallarhorn
gjallarhorn.unidentified_name: a great curved horn banded in gold
gjallarhorn.lore: Heimdall, the white god with the teeth of gold, keeps watch at the bridge Bifrost, and he needs less sleep than a bird and can hear the grass grow. This is his Gjallarhorn, the Yelling Horn, whose blast is heard in every world. At Ragnarok it shall wake the gods and bring the einherjar, Odin's chosen dead, riding out of Valhalla to the last battle. As he cannot leave his bridge he has put it in your hands, and if you blow it once they will ride beside you, though the wolf himself is not theirs to kill, nor to bind.

_meta.sources: Snorri, Gylfaginning 27 and 51; Voluspa 46; Grimnismal and Gylfaginning 38-41 on the einherjar. Grokipedia (Gjallarhorn, Heimdall, Einherjar), Wikipedia (Heimdall). The power is in data/horns.json.

raphaels_gall.name: Raphael's Gall
raphaels_gall.unidentified_name: a fish's gall wrapped in a leaf
raphaels_gall.lore: Under the name of Azarias the archangel Raphael walked with young Tobias to Media and home again, as the Book of Tobit tells, and taught him the uses of the fish that leapt at him from the Tigris. Its heart and liver drove away a demon when they were burned, and its gall restored the sight of old Tobit. This is that gall, still in its leaf. The first time that darkness would fall upon your eyes the gall will be spent, and your sight will not fail you.
